name: Stray
tested: playable on iPad, early testing (1.5, Steam).
why: cap texture streaming memory to the device's RAM: the Mac build sizes it for a GPU with its own memory; turn off capsule shadows, whose tiled pass blacks out the fog in every 16-pixel tile the cat touches on iOS (hard-edged black blocks around the cat on the title screen); render at 75% and let MetalFX's temporal upscaler fill in the rest: about 58 frames/s on the title screen of an M1 iPad Pro instead of 45, with no visible difference (50% reaches the 60 frames/s cap but only gains 2 more); decode sounds as they play instead of unpacking them on load: the Audio Mixer's CoreAudio platform does not override IAudioMixerPlatformInterface::SupportsRealtimeDecompression, whose base answer is false, so every sound in a level was unpacked to PCM (1.5 GB in chapter 4, The Slums, more than an iPhone can spare); the patch makes it answer true (mov w0, #0 -> #1) and au.ForceRealtimeDecompression applies it to every sound. Measured on the Mac build with the iPhone settings: 5.95 GB -> 4.8 GB in The Slums, sound unchanged
